title: Choose the tweezers that fit a carrier's tab slot and peel a display module's protective film
instruction: Two pairs of tweezers stand in their holders. Use the pair whose tips fit the carrier's tab slot to pull the blue protective film off the display module by its tab, while holding the loose carrier still. Lay the film on the table outside the carrier, put both pairs of tweezers back upright in their own holders, and move both hands away.
context: Display assembly benches keep several tweezers: paddle tips for handling film on open surfaces, fine tips for tight spaces. Here the film's pull tab hangs in a 6 mm slot of the assembly carrier, narrower than the robot's closed fingertips (7.9 mm), and the paddle tips (7 mm wide) cannot pass the tab's 5.6 mm notch, so only the fine-tip pair can pinch it. The robot has to pick that pair, open and close the passive spring tweezers through its own grip, and peel while the other hand keeps the unclamped carrier from sliding or lifting; then set the film aside and put the tools back. Gripper-only attempts and the paddle-tip pair release no film.
setup: Dual-YAM station on a 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m oak table, centre (0.36,0,0.7175) m, top z=0.7475 m. Arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75) m, left at +y, facing +x. A loose ABS carrier with glass display insert, total 250 g, occupies x=0.225..0.335, y=-0.21..0.14, z=0.7475..0.7645 m. Its base is 3 mm thick; display is 72 x 135 mm, x=0.244..0.316, y=-0.190..-0.055, glass top z=0.7625. Side rails are 21 mm wide; front support flange starts y=-0.049. A 12 x 6 mm slot at x=0.274..0.286, y=-0.055..-0.049 has a 14 mm depth above the base. Blue PE protective film is 66 x 130 mm at x=0.247..0.313, y=-0.185..-0.055. Its first 15 mm next to the tab (y=-0.070..-0.055) is a non-adhesive starter zone; the other 115 mm is stuck to the glass. The custom folded starter tab has an 8 x 10 x 1 mm hanging face centred at (0.28,-0.052,0.7580) m. Two 1.2 x 3 x 1 mm side connections leave a 5.6 mm central entry notch and 2.5 mm rear clearance. A 15 g stainless-steel tweezer tool, 120 mm long, has 2.4 x 0.8 mm tips and rests open 8 mm, pointing down in an ABS stand centred (0.36,-0.24). Stand floor is 30 x 34 x 3 mm; four 3 mm thick walls rise 20 mm above z=0.7505. A second, otherwise identical tool with 7 x 0.8 mm paddle tips stands open in an identical stand centred (0.36,-0.17). Both stands are fixed. Exact component bounds and the fixed starting layout are in fixture_geometry.py and tool_geometry.py.
scoring: Any carrier excursion beyond 30 mm horizontally, 5 mm vertically or 10 degrees yaw/tilt, or film seam separation beyond 3 mm, makes the trial score 0. Consecutive peeled adhesive length, from the starter zone: <30 mm: 0; >=30 mm: 0.25; >=60 mm: 0.5; >=90 mm: 0.75. Full credit requires all 115 mm of adhesive detached; every film piece at least 2 mm outside the carrier, within 30 mm above the tabletop, with table support; each tweezer tool's tip centre within 4.5 mm horizontally (inside its own stand's cavity) and 5 mm vertically of that stand's target, tilt <=5 degrees and tip opening 6-10 mm. Tools must move below 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s, no film piece may move over 2 mm or turn over 5 degrees, and both TCPs must be at least 80 mm from every task object, for 1 second.
reset_notes: Use fresh protective film and the specified folded/notched starter tab for each physical trial. Place the carrier flat and the open tool upright in the stand. Simulator reset restores all poses and adhesive joints; use object_jitter=0 and seed 0.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. Film: 26 rigid 5 mm strips (first three non-adhesive) and a rigid folded tab, 1 mm collision thickness; the tab is simulated at 3 g for stable tweezer contact. Peel-front springs (0.025 N m/rad) release above 60 degrees at 20 Hz, not fitted to measured adhesion. Each tweezer tool's halves slide on a 150 N/m spring, approximating flexure; contact alone grasps a tool. Carrier friction 0.4. No stretching, wrinkles, tearing, scratches or ESD. Tab and carrier are benchmark-designed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, step limit); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,298 steps).
